title: Real conversations
goal: Hold long, natural conversations: catch up with an old friend, sit through a family dinner switching between تون and توهان, argue about where to go and find a compromise, and plan a trip together.
intro:
This last unit puts everything together. Real conversations are long: someone tells the whole story of the last three years in one breath, the conversation jumps when an uncle walks in, two friends argue about the weekend until an elder settles it, and a plan slowly takes shape.

Two skills make that possible. First, **linking long sentences**: chaining actions with the 'having done' form (پهچي، نوڪري ڳولي، پوءِ…) and joining ideas with ان کان پوءِ, جيئن ته, ته جيئن, نه رڳو … پر, تڏهن به. Second, **switching register on the spot**: تون and يار with your friend, then — the moment his father appears — سائين, توهان and the polite verb forms, without missing a beat.

vocab.note: Also just پوءِ. With a verb: کائڻ کان پوءِ = after eating.
With a verb: نڪرڻ کان اڳ = before leaving.
Starts the reason clause: جيئن ته دير ٿي وئي آهي، … = since it's late, …
Followed by the subjunctive: … ته جيئن دير نه ٿئي = so that we're not late.
نه رڳو … پر … به = not only … but also …
After a contrast: مينهن پيو پوي، تڏهن به ويندس = it's raining, but I'll still go.
Adds impatience to a question: آخر ڇو؟ = but why?
Native Sindhi; آخرڪار means the same.
m. تفصيل سان = in detail.
Invariable. مختصر ۾ = in short.

f. The polite way to ask an elder how they are: طبيعت ڪيئن آهي؟

m. وچ ۾ = in the middle, between; وچ وارو رستو = the middle way.

grammar.title: Linking long sentences
grammar.body:
Fluent Sindhi strings ideas together instead of saying one short sentence at a time. The main tools:

**1. A chain of 'having done' forms.** Put every action except the last in the conjunctive form (stem + -ī / -e: پهچي، ڳولي، ڪري، کائي) and only the last verb gets tense: دبئي **پهچي**، نوڪري **ڳولي**، پوءِ گهر **ورتم** 'I got to Dubai, found a job, then got a place'. Don't put ۽ between them.

**2. Time order**: **ان کان پوءِ** 'after that', **ان کان اڳ** 'before that'. With a verb, use the oblique infinitive: کائڻ **کان پوءِ** 'after eating', نڪرڻ **کان اڳ** 'before leaving'.

**3. Reason and purpose**: **جيئن ته** 'since, as' gives the reason first: **جيئن ته** دير ٿي وئي آهي، هتي ئي سمهندس. **ته جيئن** 'so that' gives the purpose and takes the **subjunctive**: جلدي نڪرو **ته جيئن** ٽريفڪ ۾ نه **ڦاسو**. (Don't confuse it with جيئن ته!)

**4. Adding and contrasting**: **نه رڳو … پر … به** 'not only … but also': هن **نه رڳو** فون ڪيو، **پر** گهر **به** آيو. **تڏهن به** 'even so, still' after something that should have stopped it: ٽي ڀيرا فون ڪيم، **تڏهن به** نه کنيائين. You already know پر, ڇاڪاڻ ته, تنهن ڪري and جيتوڻيڪ (unit 14).

**In speech**, long stories are held together by fillers: پوءِ… 'so then…', ڀلا… 'well…', مطلب… 'I mean…', and by repeating the last thing said: 'پهتس. پهچي ڏٺم ته…' 'I arrived. When I arrived I saw that…'.

grammar.title: Switching register mid-conversation
grammar.body:
In one evening you may talk to a close friend, his little brother, his mother and his grandfather — and Sindhi makes you choose a level each time. The switch is instant and complete: pronoun, verb form, address word, even the fillers.

**Friend / younger** — تون, bare commands, يار / ادا:
تون ڪيئن آهين؟ · اچ، ويهه · ٻڌاءِ · ڇا ٿو چوين؟ · ڪٿي هئين؟

**Elder / stranger / anyone you respect** — توهان, -o commands (or the gentle -ijo), سائين / چاچا / ماسي / ادي:
توهان ڪيئن آهيو؟ · اچو، ويهو · ٻڌايو · ڇا ٿا چئو؟ · ڪٿي هئا؟

**Highest respect** (grandparents, scholars, a pir) — پاڻ with plural verbs (unit 18): پاڻ ڪڏهن آيا؟

**What else changes when an elder walks in:**
• Ask about **طبيعت** (health) rather than 'what's up': چاچا، طبيعت ڪيئن آهي؟
• Offer before you take: سائين، توهان به ڪجهه وٺو نه.
• Drop the slang (يار، اڙي، توبه!) and the jokes; add جي, سائين and ادب سان 'respectfully'.
• Elders, in turn, use **تون** and پٽ / ڌيءَ to you — that's warmth, not rudeness.

**Switching down** can be a sign of affection (a friend's mother may move from توهان to تون once she knows you) — but switching down in an argument is an insult. Switching **up** with a friend (اوهو، توهان ته وڏا ماڻهو ٿي ويا آهيو!) is teasing.

When in doubt, stay with **توهان**: nobody is offended by too much respect.

examples.en: Come on, mate, sit down! (to a friend)
Come in, sir, have a seat! (to an elder)
What do you say? (to a friend)
When did you arrive, sir? (very respectful)

dialogue.title: An old friend comes home
dialogue.setting: Junaid is back in Larkana after three years in Dubai. His school friend Asif invites him to dinner with his father; plans for the weekend follow.

lines.en: Junaid! After so many years! Where have you been hiding, mate?

lines.en: Listen, I've got a plan. Shall we go up to Gorakh this Friday? Cool air, great views…

lines.speaker: Junaid
lines.native: گورک؟ رستو ڏاڍو ڊگهو آهي، يار. ڪينجهر ويجهو آهي، ۽ ٻيڙيءَ ۾ به گهمي سگهون ٿا.

lines.en: Gorakh? The road's really long, mate. Keenjhar is closer, and we can go out on a boat too.

lines.speaker: Asif

lines.roman: kīnjhar ta har sāla vañūṃ thā! āxir kujhu naoṃ bi ta karyūṃ!
lines.en: We go to Keenjhar every year! Come on, let's do something new for once!

lines.speaker: Father
lines.native: جهيڙو نه ڪريو، ٻار! وچ وارو رستو ڪڍو: هن ڀيري گورک، ايندڙ ڀيري ڪينجهر.
lines.roman: jheṛo na karyo, ɓāra! vicha vāro rasto kaḍho: hin bhere gorakh, endaṛa bhere kīnjhar.
lines.en: Stop squabbling, boys! Find a middle way: Gorakh this time, Keenjhar next time.

lines.speaker: Junaid
lines.native: جيئن توهان چئو، چاچا. پر جيئن ته رستو ڊگهو آهي، صبح جو سوير نڪرنداسين.
lines.roman: jīeṃ tavhāṃ chao, chāchā. para jīeṃ ta rasto ḍigho āhe, subuh jo sver nikirandāsīṃ.
lines.en: As you say, Uncle. But since it's a long road, we'll set off early in the morning.

lines.en: Good boys. And make sure you call when you get there!

lines.speaker: Junaid
lines.native: ضرور، چاچا. نيٺ فيصلو ٿي ويو!
lines.roman: zarūr, chāchā. neṭh faisalo thī vayo!
lines.en: Of course, Uncle. At last, it's decided!

culture:
Long conversation is an art in Sindh. Every meeting opens with **حال احوال** — a ritual exchange in which you ask after the other person's health, family, children, work and village one by one, and they ask after yours. Rushing it is rude; with elders it can take minutes, and it's the moment to show warmth.

The evening **ڪچهري** — friends or neighbours sitting together over tea, often on charpais in a courtyard or at a roadside hotel — is where stories, politics, cricket and gossip flow for hours. Interrupting, talking over each other and loud laughter are normal; long silences are not.

When an elder joins, young men sit up straight, stop smoking and joking, and switch to **توهان** and **سائين** instantly; an elder's word often settles an argument, as Asif's father does here. You'll call your friends' parents **چاچا** and **ماسي**, and they'll treat you as their own child — including asking you to call when you've arrived safely.

Favourite trips from Sindh's cities include **Gorakh Hill**, Sindh's hill station above Dadu, **Keenjhar Lake** near Thatta with its boats and fried fish, the **Karoonjhar** hills of Nagarparkar, which turn green after the monsoon rains, and the Indus at Sukkur.

lessons.title: Catching up after years

tip.title: حال احوال — catching up
tip.body:
- Start with **حال احوال**: health, family, work — one by one.
- Ask for the full story: **تفصيل سان** ٻڌاءِ; give the short version: **مختصر ۾**…
- With a friend: ڪٿي گم **هئين**؟; with an elder: ڪٿي هئا؟

lessons.title: Telling it all in one go

tip.title: Linking: then, since, so that, still
tip.body:
- Chain actions: پهچي، ڳولي، **پوءِ** + one tensed verb.
- **ان کان پوءِ / ان کان اڳ** = after / before that.
- **جيئن ته** = since (reason); **ته جيئن** = so that + subjunctive.
- **نه رڳو … پر … به** = not only … but also; **تڏهن به** = still.
tip.pattern: X-ī، Y-ī، پوءِ Z · … ته جيئن + subjunctive

lessons.title: Family dinner: switching register

tip.title: تون with friends, توهان with elders
tip.body:
- Friend: **تون**، اچ، ويهه، ٻڌاءِ، يار.
- Elder: **توهان**، اچو، ويهو، ٻڌايو، سائين / چاچا.
- Ask an elder about **طبيعت**, and offer before you take.
- Highest respect: **پاڻ** + plural verb.

sentences.native: امان، توهان ويهو، مان ماني آڻيان ٿو.
sentences.roman: amāṃ, tavhāṃ veho, māṃ mānī āṇyāṃ tho.
sentences.en: Mum, you sit — I'll bring the food. (man)

sentences.native: وڏن سان ادب سان ڳالهايو.
sentences.roman: vaɗan sāṃ adaba sāṃ ɠālhāyo.
sentences.en: Speak to your elders respectfully.

sentences.native: بابا جي اڳيان ايترو مذاق نه ڪر!
sentences.roman: bābā jī aɠiyāṃ etiro mazāqu na karu!
sentences.en: Don't joke around so much in front of Dad!

sentences.native: پاڻ ڪڏهن آيا، سائين؟
sentences.roman: pāṇa kaɗahiṃ āyā, sāīṃ?
sentences.en: When did you arrive, sir? (very respectful)

sentences.native: عيد تي وڏي گڏجاڻي ٿيندي.
sentences.roman: ʿīda te vaɗī gaɗjāṇī thīndī.
sentences.en: There'll be a big get-together at Eid.

sentences.native: ماسي، توهان جي طبيعت هاڻي ڪيئن آهي؟
sentences.roman: māsī, tavhāṃ jī tabīata hāṇe kīeṃ āhe?
sentences.en: Auntie, how are you feeling now?

sentences.native: مون کي سمنڊ پسند آهي، توکي جبل!
sentences.roman: moṃ khe samunḍu pasanda āhe, tokhe jabala!
sentences.en: I like the sea, you like the mountains!

sentences.native: آخر ڇو نه؟
sentences.roman: āxir chho na?
sentences.en: Come on, why not?

sentences.native: هر ڀيري تون ئي فيصلو ڪرين ٿو!
sentences.roman: har bhere tūṃ ī faisalo kareṃ tho!
sentences.en: You always get to decide!

sentences.native: ٺيڪ آهي، سمجهوتو ڪريون.
sentences.roman: ṭhīku āhe, samjhauto karyūṃ.
sentences.en: OK, let's compromise.

sentences.native: اسان جو ٿورو جهيڙو ٿي ويو.
sentences.roman: asāṃ jo thoro jheṛo thī vayo.
sentences.en: We had a bit of a row.

sentences.native: وچ ۾ نه ڳالهاءِ!
sentences.roman: vicha meṃ na ɠālhāi!
sentences.en: Don't interrupt! (to a friend)

sentences.native: آخر تون چاهين ڇا ٿو؟
sentences.roman: āxir tūṃ chāheṃ chhā tho?
sentences.en: What do you actually want? (to a male friend)

sentences.native: حيدرآباد ڪراچيءَ ۽ سکر جي وچ ۾ آهي.
sentences.roman: haidarābād karāchīa ai sakhar jī vicha meṃ āhe.
sentences.en: Hyderabad is between Karachi and Sukkur.

sentences.native: سمجهوتي سان ئي مسئلو حل ٿيندو.
sentences.roman: samjhaute sāṃ ī masʾilo halu thīndo.
sentences.en: Only a compromise will solve the problem.

sentences.native: تنهنجي مرضي، يار. مان تيار آهيان.
sentences.roman: tunhinjī marzī, yār. māṃ tayāru āhiyāṃ.
sentences.en: Up to you, mate. I'm ready.

sentences.native: جهيڙو ڇڏيو، ماني ٿڌي ٿي رهي آهي!
sentences.roman: jheṛo chhaɗyo, mānī thadhī thī rahī āhe!
sentences.en: Stop arguing, the food's getting cold!

sentences.native: اسان جي رٿا آهي ته گورک هلون.
sentences.roman: asāṃ jī rithā āhe ta gorakh halūṃ.
sentences.en: Our plan is to go to Gorakh.

sentences.native: بجيٽ ڪيترو آهي؟
sentences.roman: bajiṭu ketiro āhe?
sentences.en: What's the budget?

sentences.native: رهائش جو ڇا ٿيندو؟
sentences.roman: rahāisha jo chhā thīndo?
sentences.en: What about somewhere to stay?

sentences.native: اتي جي هوا ڏاڍي ٿڌي آهي.
sentences.roman: ute jī havā ɗāḍhī thadhī āhe.
sentences.en: The air up there is really cool.

sentences.native: ٽڪر تان نظارو ڪمال جو آهي.
sentences.roman: ṭakara tāṃ nazāro kamāla jo āhe.
sentences.en: The view from the hill is amazing.

sentences.native: اڳواٽ ڪمرو وٺڻو پوندو.
sentences.roman: aɠvāṭu kamiro vaṭhaṇo pavando.
sentences.en: We'll have to book a room in advance.

sentences.native: بجيٽ گهٽ آهي، تنهن ڪري بس ۾ هلنداسين.
sentences.roman: bajiṭu ghaṭu āhe, tanhin kare basa meṃ halandāsīṃ.
sentences.en: The budget's tight, so we'll go by bus.

sentences.native: ڪينجهر تي ٻيڙيءَ ۾ گهمنداسين.
sentences.roman: kīnjhar te ɓeṛīa meṃ ghumandāsīṃ.
sentences.en: We'll take a boat out on Keenjhar.

sentences.native: برسات ۾ ٿر جا نظارا ڏسڻ جهڙا هوندا آهن.
sentences.roman: barsāta meṃ thara jā nazārā ɗisaṇa jhaṛā hundā āhin.
sentences.en: In the monsoon, the views in Thar are worth seeing.

sentences.native: سامان گهٽ کڻجو، ته جيئن آسان رهي.
sentences.roman: sāmānu ghaṭu khaṇijo, ta jīeṃ āsānu rahe.
sentences.en: Pack light, so it stays easy.

sentences.native: نيٺ گهر پهتاسين!
sentences.roman: neṭh ghara pahutāsīṃ!
sentences.en: Home at last!

sentences.native: مان ڏاڍو ٿڪجي پيو آهيان.
sentences.roman: māṃ ɗāḍho thakjī peyo āhiyāṃ.
sentences.en: I'm exhausted. (man)

sentences.native: هاڻي موڪلايون، دير ٿي وئي آهي.
sentences.roman: hāṇe moklāyūṃ, dera thī vaī āhe.
sentences.en: Let's say goodbye now, it's late.

sentences.native: پهچي ميسيج ڪجو.
sentences.roman: pahuchī mesej kajo.
sentences.en: Send a message when you get there.

sentences.native: ڏاڍو مزو آيو، وري ملنداسين.
sentences.roman: ɗāḍho mazo āyo, varī milandāsīṃ.
sentences.en: That was great fun — we'll meet again.

sentences.native: نيٺ تو سچ ٻڌايو!
sentences.roman: neṭh to sachu ɓudhāyo!
sentences.en: At last you told the truth! (to a friend)

sentences.native: سڄو ڏينهن هلي هلي ٿڪجي پياسين.
sentences.roman: saʄo ɗīṃhu halī halī thakjī pyāsīṃ.
sentences.en: We were worn out from walking all day.

sentences.native: پنهنجو خيال رکجانءِ، يار.
sentences.roman: panhinjo xiyālu rakhijāṃi, yār.
sentences.en: Take care of yourself, mate.

sentences.native: امان جو خيال رکجو.
sentences.roman: amāṃ jo xiyālu rakhijo.
sentences.en: Look after Mum.
